title: Workflow IR
description: The canonical intermediate representation of a discovered LLM workflow: a versioned graph of static node definitions and typed edges. Emitted by Discovery (P1); consumed by the Config Layer (P2), Pattern Classifier (P3.5), Eval (P4), Re-arrangement (P5), and the graph UI. Frozen at M0. See docs/prd/P0-foundations.md and openspec/changes/p0-foundations.
$comment: ir_version is the semantic version of THIS schema (the IR contract), not of the source repo. Referential integrity (every edge endpoint and every runtime-invocation node_id must reference an existing node) is a semantic check performed by CI beyond JSON Schema's expressive power; JSON Schema here validates structure and required fields only.

ir_version.description: Semver of the Workflow IR schema. Adding an optional field bumps MINOR; removing/renaming a field or making an optional field required bumps MAJOR (NFR1, additive evolution).

workflow.description: Identity of the source workflow the IR was extracted from.

id.description: Stable identifier for this workflow within the platform.

commit_sha.description: Exact commit the IR was extracted from; part of what makes an IR diffable and reproducible.

language.description: Primary source language of the workflow (e.g. python, typescript, go).

nodes.description: Static node definitions. Node COUNT is the length of this array (per-definition count); a definition with variable runtime fan-out is flagged variable_at_runtime, never expanded into multiple nodes (FR4).

edges.description: Typed edges between static node definitions.

subgraphs.description: Optional. Named subgraphs (a set of node_ids) for per-subgraph pattern labelling. Unset in P0/P1; populated by the P3.5 Pattern Classifier, which labels SUBGRAPHS (nodes and/or subgraphs — FR7). Absence never invalidates an IR; adding it is additive (no MAJOR bump).

declared_env.description: Optional (P10, additive). The environment variables the discovered workflow declares. A P10 `env` binding is validated against this set at spec-resolve; a variable not declared here is rejected, so an undeclared env read cannot reach a provider as an empty substitution. Adding it is additive (no MAJOR bump).

Node.title: Static node definition
Node.description: One discovered LLM call site. Exposes every dimension the Config Layer can override.

node_id.description: Stable identifier derived deterministically from the call site, so two Discovery runs over the same commit produce the same node_id (diffability).

kind.description: A node is always a static definition. Runtime execution instances are runtime-invocation records (see runtime-invocation.schema.json), not nodes.

call_site.description: Precise source anchor, sufficient for a later phase (P2 codemod) to rewrite the call site.

symbol.description: Enclosing function/method/symbol containing the call site.

ast_path.description: Optional structured path to the call expression in the AST, for robust rewrites across formatting changes.

in_scope.description: Optional (P10, additive). The symbols recorded as in scope at this call site — conservatively only those already reaching the call, never the full lexical scope. A P10 `expr` binding is validated against this set at spec-resolve; absence means the IR does not record scope and the transform's own check applies. Adding it is additive (no MAJOR bump).

model.description: The current/observed model binding at this call site.

params.description: Inference parameters (temperature, max_tokens, top_p, ...). Free-form; part of the config_hash include set.

prompt.description: The prompt at this call site: a registry template reference OR inline text, plus the declared variable slots.

template_ref.description: Reference to a versioned prompt-registry entry. Mutually exclusive with inline.

inline.description: Inline prompt text. Large prompts SHOULD be content-hashed to the blob store and referenced; see storage decision record.

variables.description: Declared variable slots the prompt interpolates.

tools_skills.description: Bound tool/skill names available at this call site. FROZEN and never repurposed: P14 split tools from skills ADDITIVELY into the optional `tools`/`skills` properties below, leaving this conflated view exactly as pre-P14 consumers read it (openspec/changes/p14-skills-tools-optimization/decisions.md D-14.1).

tools.description: Optional (P14, additive — no MAJOR bump). The provider-native tools this node offers the model, split out of the frozen `tools_skills` list. A tool is SELECTED (kept or pruned) against this discovered set, fail-closed; it is never resolved from a registry ref, because a tool is already identified by its call site (D-14.2). ABSENT means this IR predates the split, which is NOT the same as "this node offers no tools" — a consumer that conflated the two would accept a selection over nothing.

name.description: The tool's discovered call-site identifier — how a tool selection names it.

declared_at.description: Where this tool sits as a STATIC, deletable element of a written list. ABSENT is load-bearing: it means the node's tool set is assembled at runtime, so there is no declaration a prune could delete, and the transform REFUSES with ErrUnsafeRewrite rather than guessing (FR14, D-14.3). The file is the node's own call_site.file and is not repeated here.

index.description: Position in the written list, so a deletion addresses the element rather than searching for text that may appear more than once.

skills.description: Optional (P14, additive — no MAJOR bump). The registered platform capabilities this node binds, split out of the frozen `tools_skills` list. A skill is BOUND by constructing a value from its sealed contract — the opposite mechanic to a tool's selection — which is why the two cannot share one slice.

memory.description: Optional (P17, additive — no MAJOR bump). The memory strategy this node already implements: what it carries ACROSS invocations and sessions, as opposed to `context_assembly`, which is how a SINGLE call builds its message list. Absent means the document predates the field and is read as `none`. Discovery emits `none` for every node, which is a claim about the evidence rather than a placeholder: a store read and written between turns is not visible at the single call site P1 extracts, which is why `MemoryManagement` is a behavioral pattern and not a structural one.

context_assembly.description: How context is built for this call (RAG policy, message-window strategy, etc.).

invocation_semantics.description: Whether this definition fires once or a variable number of times at runtime.

type.description: single: fires once per case. loop: agent/iteration with runtime-variable count. conditional: fires zero-or-once depending on a runtime branch.

variable_at_runtime.description: true when the number of runtime LLM calls is not statically fixed (loops, conditional agents). Such a node is still exactly ONE node in the graph (FR4).

IOContract.title: Typed per-node I/O contract
IOContract.description: Required from IR v1 (FR5). Each of input_schema/output_schema is an embedded JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) describing the node's input/output shape. Early schemas MAY be permissive (e.g. {"type":"object"}) when static analysis cannot fully infer the shape; refining precision later is an additive change and does NOT bump ir_version MAJOR.

input_schema.$comment: An embedded JSON Schema 2020-12 document. Kept as a generic object here because JSON Schema cannot fully validate that arbitrary embedded content is itself a valid schema; a CI meta-validation step checks it compiles.

output_schema.$comment: An embedded JSON Schema 2020-12 document; see input_schema.

PatternLabels.title: Reserved pattern labels (P3.5)
PatternLabels.description: Optional. Unset in P0/P1; populated by the P3.5 Pattern Classifier. Absence never invalidates an IR (FR7).
PatternLabels.$comment: EXPAND step (IR 1.1.0, P3.5): source/subgraph_ref/detector_id/llm_run_ref/taxonomy_version/candidate were added as OPTIONAL properties on the reserved P0 record. Adding optional fields bumps MINOR, never MAJOR — a P0/P1 document carrying only {pattern, confidence} still validates here, which is the whole point of reserving the slot. The `pattern` enum is deliberately NOT closed in the schema: closing it would be a RESTRICTING change to a frozen contract (additive-only policy) and would retroactively invalidate the P0 sample. Taxonomy membership is enforced at write time by the classifier (internal/patternclassifier: Label.Validate), which is the layer that owns the vocabulary.

pattern.description: A pattern name from the fixed 20-pattern taxonomy (defined in P3.5).

source.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.1.0). Which layer produced the label: a deterministic structural rule detector, or the constrained LLM-as-classifier fallback.

subgraph_ref.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.1.0). The region this label applies to — a subgraph_id, or a node_id when the label is a capability co-existing on a node. Classification is PER-SUBGRAPH: a label that does not name its region cannot dispatch a metric-set.

detector_id.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.1.0). Set when source = rule: identifies the versioned structural detector that fired.

llm_run_ref.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.1.0). Set when source = llm: keys the reproducibility record {model, seed, temperature, prompt_version, taxonomy_version} for that fallback run.

taxonomy_version.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.1.0). Pins the taxonomy the label was drawn from, so the label stays interpretable if the taxonomy is later extended.

candidate.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.1.0). true when structure could only show a CANDIDATE for a behavioral pattern (e.g. a loop-back edge suggests Reflection but cannot prove the loop iterates). Behavioral confirmation is P5; such a label carries a capped confidence and is never asserted as fact.

author.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.3.0, P30 D4). WHO AUTHORED this fact: a language frontend (frontend), a rule detector or the constrained classifier fallback (detector), the platform's analysis agent (heros), or a human correction (operator). ABSENCE reads as `legacy` — the fact predates authorship being recorded — and is deliberately NOT back-filled, because back-filling would assert something about facts nobody examined. It is an ENUM rather than an is_inferred boolean so a fourth author can be added without replacing a field written into stored documents. Distinct from an edge's `provenance`, which answers the orthogonal question of evidence STRENGTH. On a label it is NOT derivable from `source`: P30's agent emits its labels through the RULE layer by design (one arbitration path), so a heros label reads source=rule.

Subgraph.title: Subgraph (P3.5 pattern-labelling unit)
Subgraph.description: A named set of node_ids the P3.5 classifier labels with agentic pattern(s). P3.5 emits a SET of labels tied to the specific subgraph — never one label for the whole workflow. Optional and reserved: unset in P0/P1.

node_ids.description: The node_ids composing this subgraph (each references a node in the nodes array; referential integrity checked in CI).

Edge.description: A typed edge between two static node definitions. Both endpoints reference existing node_ids (referential integrity checked in CI).

kind.description: data: producer output feeds consumer input. control: a router/condition activates the target without passing data.

provenance.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.2.0). How this edge was recovered: read from a declarative framework graph (framework); inferred from the source call-graph / data-flow / shared-conversation-state (inferred_static); or inferred from run traces — span parent-child / shared-thread-id / temporal (inferred_dynamic). Absence means an edge whose provenance is unrecorded and MUST be treated as framework-strength by a pre-1.2.0 consumer. An inferred edge is a HYPOTHESIS; a consumer never renders it as framework-certain.

confidence.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.2.0). Confidence in a recovered edge in [0,1]. Absent = unspecified (treat as 1.0). Meaningful for inferred_* edges; a framework edge is 1.0.

signal.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.2.0). The specific evidence the edge was recovered from (e.g. call_graph, data_flow, shared_state, span_parent, shared_thread, temporal, framework), so a reader sees WHY the edge exists, not only its provenance tier.

author.description: OPTIONAL (added in IR 1.3.0, P30 D4). WHO AUTHORED this fact: a language frontend (frontend), a rule detector or the constrained classifier fallback (detector), the platform's analysis agent (heros), or a human correction (operator). ABSENCE reads as `legacy` — the fact predates authorship being recorded — and is deliberately NOT back-filled, because back-filling would assert something about facts nobody examined. It is an ENUM rather than an is_inferred boolean so a fourth author can be added without replacing a field written into stored documents. Distinct from an edge's `provenance`, which answers the orthogonal question of evidence STRENGTH.
